Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

glyph (development version)

  • Bar and area charts now start their value axis at zero (#29). The y axis used to start at the smallest value, so the smallest bar had no height and the others weren’t in proportion to their values. Bars and areas are now drawn from zero, so a negative bar hangs down from zero instead of rising from the bottom of the plot. Histograms already started at zero. A domain set with scale() is used as given, including on the shared axes of facet() and compose(). Point and line marks are unchanged.
  • A GitHub Actions workflow runs R CMD check on Windows, macOS and Linux for every pull request, alongside the browser tests and the pkgdown site.
  • New browser tests (#28) draw plots in headless Chrome through chromote and check what was drawn: that plots draw at all, that slide-animated bars end at their full height, that the x axis stays visible in a wide, short container, box and histogram geometry, polygon vertices, one tooltip per widget after repeated resizes, widgets in knitted documents, and the “Clear selection” and “Reset zoom” buttons. They are skipped on CRAN and wherever chromote or Chrome isn’t available, and a GitHub Actions workflow runs them on every pull request. chromote, htmltools and withr are new suggested packages.
  • New “Clear selection” button in a plot’s controls bar, shown while a brush selection exists (#26). Clicking or tapping it clears the selection and restores every mark, including marks in panels linked with compose(linked_selections = TRUE). Pressing Escape clears brush selections too, unless you are typing in a text field. Plots with a brush but no zoom now get a controls bar for the button. When the controls don’t fit the plot’s width, as in small facet panels, they show just their symbols, with the full label in their tooltip.
  • “Reset zoom” and double-click zooming no longer lag on large plots (#25). They jump straight to the result instead of animating when the plot has 3,000 or more elements, since each frame of the animation redrew every point. At 15,000 points a reset now takes about 50ms instead of 470ms. Each zoom step still redraws every point, which canvas drawing (#20) is meant to fix.
  • Tooltips no longer fall behind the pointer over dense areas of a large point plot (#23). With brushing on, each pointer move used to search every point for the nearest one and move the tooltip, and in WebKit moving the tooltip repainted the plot underneath it. At 15,000 points one move took about half a second, so moves queued up and the tooltip kept changing for over a minute after the pointer stopped. Points are now found through a quadtree, pointer moves are handled at most once per frame for the latest position, and the tooltip is drawn on its own layer so moving it doesn’t repaint the plot. The same points are found as before.
  • Redrawing a plot no longer leaves old tooltips in the page. Every resize redraws the plot, and fitting it to its container can take up to three draws, and each draw added another tooltip for every mark with one, plus click listeners that kept the replaced plot in memory. A faceted plot resized ten times left 144 tooltips behind, and a tooltip showing when the plot was redrawn could stay on screen. Each widget now has one tooltip, which a redraw hides and reuses.
  • Plots with many rows are much quicker to prepare (#8). Plot data now goes to the browser as one array per column instead of one object per row, and is turned back into rows in the browser before anything is drawn. Each row is sent once: a mark that draws the plot’s own data refers to it instead of carrying a second copy. Boxplot, violin and histogram marks send their summaries and the row indices that brushing and linked selections use, not the raw rows. At 100,000 points compile() takes 0.1s instead of 65s, the widget is ready for the Viewer in 0.4s, and the file is 5 MB instead of 14 MB. Plots look and behave as before.
  • The compiled JSON (compile()$json and export(..., "plot.json")) has a new data layout, marked by "$schema": "glyph/v0.2". Data is {"columns": {...}, "n": rows}, and a mark that draws the plot’s data has {"from": "plot", "fields": [...], "rows": [...]}, where rows is null or lists the 0-based rows it keeps after dropping missing values. Boxplot, violin, histogram and polygon marks send {"values": [...]}, one record per box, violin, bin or shape.
  • New mark_polygon() draws closed shapes from x/y vertices, one per value of group (#7). Vertices are joined in row order, color fills each shape, style sets the fill, outline colour, outline width and opacity, and radius rounds the corners. Each polygon is one element: it gets one tooltip, and brushing or clicking it selects all of its rows, including in linked panels. It works with facet(), compose(), zoom, theme tokens, computed mappings and NA dropping.
  • Boxplot, violin, sina and histogram marks no longer leave out rows whose colour is missing. Those rows now form a group of their own.
  • Plots now fit inside their container in both directions (#17). A plot was drawn at the spec’s width and height (600 x 400 unless set) and scaled to the container’s width, so in a wide, short container such as RStudio’s Viewer pane it came out taller than the space available and its x axis was cut off. The same happened to facet() grids, which also overflowed narrow containers, and plots in R Markdown documents ran past their 400px box into the text below. Plots and facet grids are now drawn at the size of the container they are in, and are redrawn when it is resized.
  • New statistical marks (#6): mark_boxplot(), mark_violin(), mark_sina() and mark_histogram(). Their statistics are computed in R when the plot is compiled, with stats::quantile(), stats::density() and hist()-style bins, after computed mappings are evaluated and rows with missing values are dropped. They work with facet() (summaries are computed per panel), compose(), theme tokens, tooltips (which show the statistics), hover, click and brushing. Each box, violin or bin knows which rows it summarises, so brushing points or linked panels highlights the boxes and bins that contain the selected rows, and brushing a box selects its rows.
  • Brushing and zooming now apply to the whole plot rather than to each point mark separately. A plot with several brushable marks gets one brush that covers all of them, and interact(zoom = TRUE) now zooms plots that have no point mark.
  • Points on a categorical x axis are now drawn in the middle of their category instead of at its left edge.
  • A quantitative axis now spans the values of every mark in the plot, not just the first, so a second mark with a wider range is no longer cut off.
  • Automatic tooltips show a computed mapping by its expression (e.g. factor(cyl)) instead of its internal column name, and tooltip templates can refer to fields whose names contain dots, such as {.median}.
  • Plots and layouts now draw automatically in R Markdown, Quarto and vignettes, without ending the pipeline with render() (#13). glyph registers knit_print() methods for glyph_spec and glyph_layout; knitr stays a suggested package. Printing a compose() layout at the console now draws it, the same as a single plot, and the text description it used to print is available from the new summary.glyph_layout(). render() is still there for setting the width and height.
  • Rewrote the README, the pkgdown home page, ARCHITECTURE.md and the Getting Started vignette in plainer language (#4).
  • Removed the comparisons with ggplot2 from the documentation, including the comparison tables in the README and the “glyph vs ggplot2” vignette. The package Title and Description now describe what glyph does (#5).
  • The help pages no longer compare glyph with other packages either, and several now describe the code more accurately. ?glyph no longer claims that lists, URLs or Arrow tables are accepted as data, ?facet no longer says panels get independent scales by default, and ?marks and ?interactivity drop features that don’t exist (#5).
  • export() to .html no longer fails on machines without pandoc (#3). Instead of a low-level pandoc error, it now writes the HTML with its JavaScript in a <name>_files folder alongside, and says so, including how to get a single self-contained file (install pandoc, or run inside RStudio). The pandoc requirement is now documented in ?export.
  • Fixed the entrance/slide animation for bar charts showing no bars on Safari and Chrome mobile (#2). The animation was reading a value that was never set and had already been zeroed out, so bars always animated to zero height; it now stores each bar’s real height/position before animating.
  • Made plots responsive: the SVG now scales to fill its container (via viewBox) instead of a fixed 600px width, and the theme background now always covers the full plot area. Previously a dark theme’s background didn’t reach the edges on narrower or wider containers, including on mobile.
  • Added a reset-zoom control, and made double-tap reset the zoom instead of always zooming in further, so a zoomed-in plot can be zoomed back out on touch devices.
  • Tooltips now also appear on tap and dismiss on tapping elsewhere, for touch devices that have no hover state.
  • Brush selection now also clears on a tap outside the plot, not just on a no-drag tap inside it.
  • Fixed tapping/clicking a point doing nothing when both brush and tooltip/click interactions were enabled on the same mark: the brush’s full-plot overlay sits on top of the marks (so a drag can start from anywhere) and was swallowing the tap before it reached the point underneath.
  • Fixed the same problem for continuous mouse hover: hovering over a point did nothing (no tooltip, no hover effect) whenever brush was also enabled on that mark, for the same reason as the tap fix above. Brushing itself still works by dragging from anywhere in the plot area.
  • Fixed one drag both panning and brushing when zoom and brush were enabled on the same mark: zoom binds its drag to the <svg> and brush to an overlay inside it, so a single mousedown started both gestures. A drag now does one thing at a time — it brushes by default when brushing is available, and a small toggle next to the reset-zoom control (shown only when both are enabled) switches dragging between selecting and panning. The scroll wheel, a trackpad pinch, a two-finger pinch and a double-click/double-tap always zoom, whichever mode the toggle is in.
  • Two-finger pinch-zoom now works on plots that also have brush enabled. d3-brush stops propagation of every touch move once its one-finger gesture starts, so a second finger never reached the zoom behavior; the pinch is now handled before anything can intercept it.
  • Fixed the plot jumping by its axis-margin offset the first time it was zoomed or panned — the zoom transform replaced the plot group’s existing margin translate instead of composing with it.
  • Clicking the reset-zoom control no longer discards the brush selection.
  • Tapping the plot’s margin (inside the chart but outside the plot area) now clears the brush selection, as tapping outside the widget already did.
  • Double-tap zoom/reset on touch no longer depends on d3-zoom’s internal gesture detection, which also makes it work for repeated double-taps and while dragging is set to brushing.
  • Computed aesthetic mappings (e.g. x = log(wt), color = factor(cyl)) are now evaluated at compile time instead of being silently dropped; the expression text is used as the default axis/legend label.
  • Rows with NA in a mapped position aesthetic (x, y, x2, y2, y_min, y_max) are now dropped for that mark at compile time, with a warning reporting how many rows were removed and from which aesthetic(s), similar to ggplot2.
  • facet(rows =, cols =) now accepts a computed expression (e.g. facet(cols = factor(cyl))), evaluated the same way as an aesthetic mapping — previously the raw expression text was used as a literal (nonexistent) column name, so faceting on anything but a plain column silently produced a single, unlabeled facet.
  • Faceted panels now use each mark’s own resolved data — computed mapping columns and NA-dropped rows included — instead of an unfiltered slice of the shared data, so facet() combined with a computed mapping or with NA values now behaves the same as the unfaceted case.
  • Removed the auto-selection of a “canvas” or “webgl” rendering engine by data size in compile() — no such renderer has ever existed, only the D3/SVG renderer does, so the “selection” never did anything. compile(engine = ...) now only accepts "auto"/"html" and errors on other values instead of silently accepting them.
  • Removed remaining claims of WebGL/Canvas rendering and standalone static SVG export from the package description, documentation, README, and ARCHITECTURE.md; a Canvas renderer is planned for a future release.
  • Added Mike Bostock to Authors@R and inst/COPYRIGHTS to credit the bundled D3.js library (ISC license), per CRAN policy for bundled JavaScript.
  • Added an “Acknowledgements” section to the README and the glyph-package help page, crediting the prior art glyph’s design draws on.
  • Documented mark_text(smart_repel = TRUE)’s actual method (iterative pairwise nudging of overlapping label boxes) instead of leaving it unspecified, and credited ggrepel as the inspiration.
  • Fixed roxygen warnings that were silently skipping the summary.glyph_spec and print.glyph_layout help topics for lacking a title.

glyph 0.1.1

CRAN release: 2026-07-08

  • Fixed critical rendering bug where interactive plots displayed as blank in RStudio viewer, R Markdown documents, and Shiny apps. Data was being serialized in column-oriented format instead of the row-records format expected by the ‘D3.js’ frontend.
  • Added error surfacing in the htmlwidget so JavaScript failures display a visible error message instead of a silent blank div.
  • Added sizing policy for better default widget dimensions in R Markdown and pkgdown contexts.

glyph 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-07-06

  • Initial CRAN release.
  • Core spec builder with quosure-based aesthetic mappings (no aes() required).
  • Eight mark types: mark_point(), mark_line(), mark_bar(), mark_area(), mark_text(), mark_rule(), mark_ribbon(), mark_link().
  • First-class interactivity via interact(): tooltips, zoom, brush selection, hover effects, cross-filtering, and named selections.
  • Declarative animation via animate(): entrance transitions and keyframe animation through data states.
  • Unified scale system via scale() with convenience wrappers scale_color(), scale_log(), scale_time().
  • Token-based theming via theme_tokens() with five built-in presets: light, dark, minimal, publication, presentation.
  • Built-in layout composition via compose(), marginals(), inset(), and facet().
  • Compilation pipeline via compile(), rendering to interactive HTML widgets via D3.js.
  • JSON spec export via export() and Vega-Lite interoperability via to_vegalite().
  • D3.js v7 rendering engine via ‘htmlwidgets’.
